description: Registry of case studies and publications. The Case Studies & Publications grid on index.html is written from this file; scripts/build_cases.py generates one reader page per entry under cases/.

fields.id: Must match the filename prefix, e.g. CS-2026-001
fields.title: Card title, 60 characters or fewer
fields.category: marketplace | payments | merchant-risk | aml | ato | forensics | methodology | trust-and-safety | ai-governance | other
fields.summary: One or two sentences, 240 characters or fewer
fields.chips: Two or three short labels shown on the card
fields.url: Markdown source, relative to the repository root
fields.page: Generated reader page, written by scripts/build_cases.py

entries.title: Payment-Direction Deception on a Classifieds Marketplace
entries.summary: A seller was contacted within minutes of listing an item and sent two images implying a payment had arrived. Neither showed a credit. Checking the balance instead of the screenshot is what stopped it.

entries.title: What a Payment-Risk Reviewer Wants From an Onboarding Pack
entries.summary: Most merchant onboarding rejections are evidence problems, not business-model problems. A five-layer assessment and one well-built pack answer the four questions a reviewer actually asks.

entries.title: A Fraud Signal Taxonomy That Survives an Audit
entries.summary: Signals drift into folklore when nobody owns their definitions. Seven categories, a stated reason for every weight, and a version stamp turn a signal list into an auditable asset.

entries.title: Six Questions a Payment-Fraud Dashboard Should Answer
entries.summary: Most fraud dashboards report activity. The useful ones answer six questions — and the last two, what did we miss and what did we get wrong, are the ones that separate a status screen from a control.
